newsitem.title: GERMANY: Air NZ/United link not seen hitting Star Alliance.
newsitem.headline: Air NZ/United link not seen hitting Star Alliance.

text.p: The debut of the alliance between United Airlines and Air New Zealand will have no immediate impact on Star Alliance, the global grouping of five major airlines, which includes United, a spokesman said on Thursday.
The spokesman for Lufthansa, a member of Star Alliance, said: "This has no initial bearing on the Star Alliance."
"There are existing bi-lateral agreements between members of the Star Alliance and other airlines and they will remain, but Star Alliance is more of a strategic alliance."
Star Alliance was launched on Wednesday and, as well as United and Lufthansa, includes Air Canada, Scandinavian Airlines Systems, Thai Airways International Ltd and Brazil's Varig Airlines.
Speculation about who will be next to join the alliance has been rife since long before the alliance finally hit the runway in a glitzy opening ceremony in Frankfurt on Wednesday.

The alliance between United and Air New Zealand began on Thursday morning with an early flight between Auckland and Melbourne on a United Airlines Boeing 747-400 aircraft, which was carrying passengers from both carriers.
But the Lufthansa spokesman dismissed speculation that the timing of the launch of the code-sharing agreement signalled a possibility that Air New Zealand could soon become part of the alliance.
"The start date is pure coincidence and I can tell you that Air New Zealand is not part of the Star Alliance," he said.
Australasia is under-represented in the alliance as it currently stands, and analysts have speculated that a move onto that continent is a possibility.
The partners in Star Alliance said at the launch that other potential partners include South African Airways and regional European carrier British Midland, which both now cooperate with Lufthansa.
Talks were also being held with unspecified Asian airlines to strengthen the alliance's presence in the expanding region but alliance airline executives declined further comment.

"Asia is the fastest growing region in terms of air traffic growth. Looking to the future of the alliance, we are hopeful there will be other airlines in that region who join," Lufthansa chief executive Juergen Weber told reporters at the launch on Wednesday.
Alliance chiefs would not comment on the possibility of Cathay Pacific -- an airline seen as strategically important in the Asian market -- joining the alliance.
Industry analysts have said Asia is a critical market and said there was no doubt partnerships will be formed there.
